run.question: Our analytics dashboard seems slow. Can you check the shard configuration for the app-186-shard-analytics index? How many primary shards does it have and what is their status?

report.summary: The exact index app-186-shard-analytics exists and its shard configuration is unambiguous: it has 7 primary shards, 0 replicas, and all 7 primaries are in state STARTED on a single node (bea971fdc0c6, 172.17.0.2); the cluster and the index both report status green with 0 unassigned, 0 initializing and 0 relocating shards. So the shard layout is healthy, not degraded, as observed at the moment of these queries (2026-11-23T17:38Z, i.e. at the end of the authorized window, not during it). The same snapshot is counter-evidence against shard configuration being the cause of dashboard slowness: the index holds 1 document total (store 6143 bytes, primary total_size_in_bytes 4554), its cumulative indexing counter index_total is 1, and its cumulative search counters query_total and fetch_total are both 0, so this index had served no search requests since creation as of the query time. No fault, misconfiguration or impact was observed on this index, so no root cause is named. The reported dashboard slowness itself was not measured here: no latency baseline or per-window query latency for this index was obtained, so whether the dashboard is actually slow, and why, remains an open question outside what the checked evidence shows.

claims.text: Index app-186-shard-analytics exists with pri=7 and rep=0, health green, status open, docs.count=1, store.size=454b.

The _cat/shards view of app-186-shard-analytics returns exactly 7 rows, all with prirep=p, shard numbers 0 through 6, every one in state STARTED on node bea971fdc0c6 (ip 172.17.0.2); shards 3 and 6 each show 227b store, the other five show 0b, and only shard 5 shows docs=1.

Cluster docker-cluster and index app-186-shard-analytics both report status green: for the index, number_of_shards=7, active_primary_shards=7, active_shards=7, unassigned_shards=0, unassigned_primary_shards=0, initializing_shards=0, relocating_shards=0, number_of_replicas=0; the cluster has number_of_data_nodes=1, number_of_nodes=1.

Against shard configuration or shard-level load explaining dashboard slowness for this index: its cumulative stats at query time show docs.count=1, store size_in_bytes=6143, indexing index_total=1 with index_time_in_millis=0, and search query_total=0, fetch_total=0, query_time_in_millis=0, open_contexts=0 — i.e. 7 primaries and 0 replicas serving one document and no recorded search traffic.

If the analytics dashboard's slowness involves this index, the cause is more likely outside its shard layout (e.g. another index, or the dashboard/query layer), because this index is green, fully allocated, and essentially empty; this remains unverified since no dashboard-side latency or query data was examined.

With number_of_replicas=0 and a single data node, all 7 primaries live on one node, so read work cannot be spread across nodes or failed over; this is a configuration characteristic that could matter under real load but is not shown to be causing an observed problem here.

To answer the slowness question rather than the shard-layout question, collect per-window search latency and search-rate measurements for the indices the dashboard actually queries, and compare against a baseline period; the current tools returned only point-in-time cluster/index state and cumulative counters.

gaps: All Elasticsearch answers used here are point-in-time snapshots taken at ~2026-11-23T17:38Z (the end of the authorized window); these tools have no time range, so the shard states and health during the incident period within 2026-10-24T17:38Z–2026-11-23T17:38Z are unknown.

No latency measurement for the dashboard or for queries against app-186-shard-analytics was obtained; the reported slowness was not verified, and no comparable baseline was available to infer a trend.

The index's cumulative search.query_total=0 shows no search traffic recorded for this index since its creation as of query time, but it does not identify which index or service the dashboard actually queries, so that link is unknown.
Whether the index had a different shard or replica configuration earlier in the window is unknown; only current settings were read.
change_history is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment or configuration-change record could be checked.
next_steps: Query per-window search latency and rate (search.query_time_in_millis/query_total deltas, or Elasticsearch slow-log/search stats) for the indices the analytics dashboard targets, against a pre-incident baseline.
Confirm which index/alias the analytics dashboard reads, since app-186-shard-analytics holds one document and shows no search traffic.
If read scalability is a concern, evaluate adding replicas or data nodes; with number_of_replicas=0 on a single data node there is no read fan-out or redundancy.
